summary: George Berrington looked at retention and expansion with Chris and Leanne. Meridian rarely gets a second site or a second portfolio company from the same PE house without the operating partner pushing it. We agreed account plans for the three core PE houses and a structured close-out review on every engagement.

discussion.keyPoints: Leanne's map showed the three core PE houses own 41 manufacturers between them; Meridian has worked with 9.
Engagements end with a final report but no formal review with the operating partner, so results are not captured as proof.
Chris noted one core PE house is raising a new fund and may change operating partners, which could cut off work.

recommendations.recommendation: Write an account plan for each of the three core PE houses with a named Meridian partner owner and a target of 2 new portfolio companies each per year.
Hold a close-out review with the operating partner on every engagement, scoring results against the agreed EBITDA bridge.
Offer a 6-month sustainment retainer at £8k a month after each 100-day plan.
Ask every operating partner with a close-out score of 8 or more to act as a reference.

actions.action: Draft the first account plan for the largest PE house

nextFocus: Model the economics behind the new pricing, acquisition and retention choices.
nextPreparation: Chris to bring utilisation, day rates and margin by engagement for the last year.

tests.question: What did we agree for key accounts?
What happens at the end of every engagement?
